behaviors.precondition: An editable scene has either a selected target node, a scene root, or an existing usable PVController; the game is not running.
behaviors.public_action: Invoke the registered Flow F4 action or the equivalent Enter Flow button.
behaviors.expected_result: Flujo reuses one compatible controller or creates exactly one undoable scene-owned PVController, selects it, and enters FLOW; Undo and Redo preserve the scene history.
invariants: No duplicate controller is created by repeated requests.
GAME never consumes F4 for editor interaction.
A second F4 leaves FLOW without deleting the controller.

behaviors.precondition: The Flow dock has less vertical space than the complete selected-item editor requires.
behaviors.public_action: Scroll the Flow dock with its native vertical ScrollContainer.
behaviors.expected_result: The vertical range exceeds the visible page and the final configuration controls can be brought fully into view.
invariants: One vertical scroll surface contains the complete configuration area.
Horizontal resizing remains native and unconstrained.
Selection and model state are not changed by scrolling.

behaviors.precondition: A schema 3 collection row or one of its public editor controls is active.
behaviors.public_action: Use public selection, Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Escape, F2, popup, Move, Undo, or Redo interactions.
behaviors.expected_result: The selected stable ID and current dock context remain aligned while focus follows only deliberate user navigation.
invariants: Selection identity never depends on the visible name or row index.
Rebuilds do not retain callbacks to detached controls.
Automatic model changes do not steal focus from unrelated editor controls.

behaviors.precondition: A Flow collection row remains semantically selected while keyboard focus belongs to another editor control.
behaviors.public_action: Move focus away from the selected ItemList without changing selection.
behaviors.expected_result: The stable-ID selection remains semantically active; a stronger cross-theme visual shade is explicitly deferred.
invariants: No focus is stolen to manufacture a visual indication.
Operations continue to target the selected stable ID.

behaviors.area: Delete, Undo, Redo, selection, and focus
behaviors.precondition: A deletable Method, Variable, Process, Timer, or supported block is selected through the real Inspector/plugin/dock path.
behaviors.public_action: Confirm Delete, then invoke scene-context Undo and Redo.
behaviors.expected_result: Delete chooses the same-index successor or prior final row, Undo selects the restored item, Redo restores the replacement, and an empty collection clears the editor.
invariants: The model and visible selected row refer to the same stable ID.
Focus is preserved only when the operation originated in that interface.
The command remains in the owning PVController scene history.
behaviors.notes: The focal verifies stable-ID row and dock recovery across Inspector-property replacement for Delete, Undo, and Redo, including focus ownership and teardown.

behaviors.precondition: A schema 2 FlowGraph satisfies its source validator and any legacy constructor payload receives the required explicit confirmation in chained steps.
behaviors.public_action: Call FlowGraphMigrator.migrate_schema_2_to_5().
behaviors.expected_result: The public 2→3→4→5 chain returns an independent validated schema 5 candidate and never mutates its source.
invariants: Every schema boundary remains explicit.
IDs, order, null positions, Variables, and invalid literal references are preserved according to their contracts.
A rejected step publishes no partial candidate.

behaviors.precondition: A runtime PVController enters a SceneTree with a valid schema 5 class definition or prepared inherited layout.
behaviors.public_action: Read, write, or reset an enabled INSTANCE attribute by stable ID and requester class ID.
behaviors.expected_result: Each controller owns an independent deeply detached value initialized from its definition default.
invariants: Definitions are never mutated.
Exact type, nullability, visibility, READONLY, and CONST rules are deterministic.
No Node, Resource, Callable, or static process-global store is retained.

behaviors.precondition: Controllers in one SceneTree resolve the same schema 5 declaring class.
behaviors.public_action: Acquire the class store and read, write, or reset a CLASS attribute by stable ID.
behaviors.expected_result: Controllers share one value only within SceneTree plus declaring class ID, retain it across scene changes, and lose it when that SceneTree ends.
invariants: Different SceneTrees and class IDs never share state.
A derived handle routes inherited CLASS slots to the declaring-class store.
Conflicting metadata rejects without resetting existing values.

behaviors.area: Schema 5 inherited attribute layout and access
behaviors.precondition: The active schema 5 graph and its saved ancestors resolve through a valid portable FlowClassCatalog.
behaviors.public_action: Resolve FlowRuntimeAttributeLayout and access slots with requester_class_id.
behaviors.expected_result: The effective layout is base→derived, each slot retains declaring_class_id, and access follows PUBLIC, PROTECTED, and PRIVATE rules.
invariants: A repeated stable ID anywhere in the hierarchy is an error.
A PRIVATE name on either side is an independent slot; PUBLIC/PROTECTED homonyms remain rejected.
Missing bases, cycles, excessive depth, and locator conflicts reject deterministically without mutation.

behaviors.precondition: An enabled PVController with a validated schema 3 graph enters the SceneTree.
behaviors.public_action: Allow PVController startup to invoke the Ready executor.
behaviors.expected_result: Enabled Ready processes execute their supported blocks once and emit console plus structured output in authored order.
invariants: Unsupported or invalid blocks are diagnosed and later blocks continue.
Definitions remain immutable.
Schema 5 never enters the schema 3 executor.

behaviors.precondition: A validated schema 3 container is executed with blocks using the default continuation or an ephemeral navigation decision.
behaviors.public_action: Execute the container through FlowReadyExecutor.
behaviors.expected_result: CONTINUE preserves linear order; JUMP resolves a stable target ID in the same container; STOP ends that path; invalid targets and accidental loops stop deterministically.
invariants: Existing output and method blocks retain default CONTINUE behavior.
The executor resolves navigation generically without knowing a concrete control-block type.
Navigation decisions and context are runtime-only and do not change schema or persistence.

behaviors.precondition: A valid schema 3 output-block container is authored through the normal Flujo Add controls.
behaviors.public_action: Add Custom Hello, persist and reload the graph or scene, then start the owning PVController.
behaviors.expected_result: The same registered concrete block survives persistence and emits Hola desde un bloque personalizado through the normal structured runtime output.
invariants: Print and Everything Flows continue through the same FlowOutputBlock execution contract.
The editor and executor contain no Custom-specific branch or dedicated control.
Stable block IDs, concrete script type, order, null positions, and schema 3 compatibility are preserved.

behaviors.precondition: An enabled schema 3 Timer has a finite positive interval and its PVController is enabled in the SceneTree.
behaviors.public_action: Start controller runtime and emit the internal Timer timeout.
behaviors.expected_result: One-shot or repeating Timers execute supported blocks in order and clean up their internal Timer nodes at shutdown.
invariants: Invalid or disabled Timers never start.
Runtime Timer nodes are not persisted into the authored scene.
Ready and Timer share the structured output boundary.

behaviors.precondition: A schema 3 PVController starts with enabled legacy Constructor blocks.
behaviors.public_action: Run the guarded controller startup sequence.
behaviors.expected_result: Constructor blocks execute exactly once immediately before Ready.
invariants: This is not Godot native _init.
Method calls inside Constructor remain unsupported and are skipped diagnostically.
Schema 4 and schema 5 declarative Constructor data is never executed through this path.

behaviors.precondition: A Ready or Timer Call Method block references an enabled starter Method by stable ID.
behaviors.public_action: Execute the containing Ready or Timer blocks.
behaviors.expected_result: The referenced Method executes its supported blocks once and returns control to the caller's next block.
invariants: Renaming does not alter the stable reference.
Missing, invalid, disabled, nested, or signature-bearing targets are diagnosed and skipped.
Arguments, returns, recursion, and method-to-method calls remain deferred.

behaviors.precondition: A v1 package manifest and its block descriptors are represented in memory without package discovery.
behaviors.public_action: Construct and validate FlowPackageManifest and FlowExternalBlockDescriptor values.
behaviors.expected_result: Valid required fields preserve order and derive package_id:type_id; empty, mismatched, duplicate, null, and unsupported-version data is rejected deterministically.
invariants: The descriptor layer does not parse JSON, discover packages, load scripts, instantiate blocks, or modify FlowBlockRegistry.
No IF-specific type, editor control, schema change, or runtime executor dependency is introduced.
The approved manifest fields are the only represented package contract in this foundation.

behaviors.precondition: A project-owned flow_packages fixture contains package directories and v1 manifest JSON files, including invalid siblings.
behaviors.public_action: Run FlowPackageManifestLoader.discover() against the project package root.
behaviors.expected_result: Packages are processed by sorted package_id, valid manifests and ordered descriptors are returned, and invalid packages produce deterministic diagnostics without preventing valid siblings.
invariants: Only manifest metadata is parsed; script existence, inheritance, loading and instantiation are deferred.
Relative script paths cannot escape their package through parent traversal.
The loader does not modify FlowBlockRegistry, editor state, runtime execution, schemas or package files.

behaviors.precondition: A metadata-valid package manifest references scripts inside its package, including valid and invalid resources.
behaviors.public_action: Run FlowExternalBlockScriptValidator.validate() for the discovered manifest.
behaviors.expected_result: Existing, loadable scripts deriving from FlowBlock are accepted; missing, non-Script, invalid, and non-FlowBlock resources receive deterministic diagnostics while later descriptors continue.
invariants: Validation uses script metadata and the existing get_base_script chain without retaining or registering instances.
No external type name, IF block, registry entry, editor control, runtime execution, or schema change is introduced.
Accepted descriptors remain in manifest order and diagnostics retain stable paths and package:type IDs.

behaviors.precondition: Integrated Registry entries and metadata/script-validated external manifests are available as ephemeral discovery results.
behaviors.public_action: Combine FlowBlockRegistry entries with valid external descriptors for authoring queries.
behaviors.expected_result: Integrated Print, Everything Flows, and Custom Hello entries remain first; valid external entries follow by package and manifest order with package:type_id keys.
invariants: Invalid metadata packages and invalid external scripts are excluded without preventing valid packages.
FlowBlockRegistry remains an integrated-block factory and contains no external package references.
The catalog does not modify popup/editor controls, instantiate blocks, execute runtime code, change schema, or know IF.

behaviors.precondition: A catalog entry comes from a metadata- and script-validated external descriptor inside a project-owned package.
behaviors.public_action: Ask FlowExternalBlockFactory to create one block from the external catalog entry.
behaviors.expected_result: The factory resolves and revalidates the declared script, calls Script.new(), returns a FlowBlock with a fresh stable ID and the descriptor display name, and rejects stale or non-external entries deterministically.
invariants: Each creation returns an independent instance and ID; no instance is retained, registered, executed, or serialized by the factory.
FlowBlockRegistry, FlowReadyExecutor, schema persistence, editor controls, and IF remain unaware of external creation.
A missing, invalid, unavailable, non-instantiable, or non-FlowBlock script produces diagnostics without affecting other catalog entries.

behaviors.area: Generic external block validation and duplication hooks
behaviors.precondition: A FlowGraph contains a FlowBlock subclass with optional structure checks or ID-addressed internal references.
behaviors.public_action: Validate the graph or duplicate it through the existing FlowGraph model API.
behaviors.expected_result: FlowBlock receives a validation context during graph validation and the complete old-ID → new-ID map during duplication; the base hooks remain no-op.
invariants: Existing built-in blocks retain their validation, persistence, and duplication behavior.
External hooks do not add schema fields, package registration, executor knowledge, or FlowIfBlock-specific behavior.
Stable IDs, ordering, null positions, and the source graph remain protected during duplication.

behaviors.precondition: A coordinator result contains one candidate Gota payload and may contain operational text around it.
behaviors.public_action: Parse the coordinator output through parse_gota_output().
behaviors.expected_result: Exactly one complete, line-delimited Gota result is accepted as strict JSON and validated against its protocol model; malformed, ambiguous, duplicate-key, non-finite, overflow, or framing-invalid payloads are rejected deterministically.
invariants: Delimiter tokens are recognized only as complete lines.
The JSON text between delimiters has no blank framing line or leading/trailing framing whitespace; free text remains allowed before BEGIN and after END.
Every JSON object rejects duplicate keys instead of applying last-value-wins semantics.
The historical flow_coordinator.Checkpoint remains distinct from GotaCheckpoint.
Cross-field request_id semantics remain owned by Python validation because standard JSON Schema cannot express them portably.

behaviors.precondition: A coordinator caller provides an explicit agent, prompt, existing directory, and positive timeout to a configured OpenCode executable.
behaviors.public_action: Call OpenCodeRunner.run() with the configured model and variant.
behaviors.expected_result: The runner builds one shell-free argv, captures stdout, stderr, and exit status, supervises one execution in a unique externally managed systemd --user cgroup on Fedora/Linux, terminates a timed-out unit with bounded cleanup, and accepts a payload only when exit code is zero and parse_gota_output() validates it.
invariants: Prompt, agent, model, and variant remain argument data even when they contain spaces, Unicode, or shell metacharacters.
GIT_PAGER and PAGER are forced to cat in the child environment without mutating the parent environment.
cwd is scoped to the child process and the runner never changes the Python process directory.
The five process and payload outcomes remain distinguishable with captured diagnostic information.
On Fedora/Linux, one unique flow-gota-*.service is created through systemd --user with KillMode=control-group; the coordinator remains outside the execution cgroup and is never made a subreaper.
The execution cgroup, not PPid, process names, process groups, or global scans, identifies forked, double-forked, setsid, reparented, and stopped descendants for timeout cleanup.
Timeout cleanup requests SIGTERM through systemd, applies a fixed grace, then requests cgroup SIGKILL and boundedly collects the unit without depending on the wrapper cooperating.
Post-timeout stdout/stderr collection remains bounded when descendants keep the captured pipes open.
Linux without a responsive systemd user manager fails clearly instead of using an insecure fallback; other operating systems retain only the existing bounded process-group termination fallback.
The minimal wrapper is the service main process, starts the target without a shell, inherits stdout/stderr, and propagates normal target exit status; it is not the security boundary.
The prompt, including shell metacharacters, environment references, quotes, Unicode, and newlines, remains literal data because systemd argument expansion is disabled.
The runner does not write SQLite or transition coordinator task state.
The approved flujo.gota/v1 parser and validation rules remain unchanged.

behaviors.precondition: A clean Git repository is on the requested branch at the requested base SHA, and an injected OpenCodeRunner-compatible boundary is available.
behaviors.public_action: Call GotaReviewCycle.run() with a worker-phase GotaRequest.
behaviors.expected_result: One Worker execution is followed by independent read-only Git verification and, only when verification passes, one gota-reviewer execution bound to the exact verified commit; both executions require status SUCCEEDED and exit_code exactly 0, and the result exposes validated payloads, a decision only for an accepted review, phase, and diagnostics.
invariants: Worker timeout, startup or containment failure, non-zero exit, contradictory SUCCEEDED/non-zero exit_code, invalid payload, invalid WorkerResult, invalid commit, branch change, dirty worktree, multiple commits, or changed-path mismatch never invokes Reviewer.

Git verification requires the declared commit to be a real descendant of the captured base, exactly one commit from that base, HEAD equality, expected branch, clean worktree, and exact changed_paths after order normalization.

Reviewer receives the captured base SHA, exact verified commit SHA, consistent task/run/request identity, and a read-only instruction; only a validated ReviewResult with matching identity, phase, and commit is accepted, and a decision is hidden when any later cycle validation fails.
Reviewer HEAD, branch, worktree, or any observable ref under refs/ mutation invalidates the cycle even when the payload decision is PASSED.
Reviewer status SUCCEEDED with an exit_code other than exactly 0 invalidates the cycle and exposes no decision.
The cycle does not transition TaskRun, write SQLite, mutate protocol schemas, or use the historical GitTransaction boundary.

behaviors.precondition: A clean Git repository is on the requested branch at the requested base SHA, and an injected OpenCodeRunner-compatible boundary is available.
behaviors.public_action: Call WorkerPhase.run() once and pass its verified VerifiedWorkerCommit to a separate ReviewPhase.run() call.
behaviors.expected_result: WorkerPhase executes and independently verifies one Worker commit into an immutable VerifiedWorkerCommit; the separate ReviewPhase treats every received handoff as untrusted, validates the Worker execution, payload, identity, Git metadata, and wrapper invariants before executing only gota-reviewer against that exact commit, and exposes a validated PASSED review without rerunning Worker.
invariants: VerifiedWorkerCommit preserves the task/run/attempt identity, base SHA, repository, branch, verified commit SHA, verified changed paths, Worker execution/result, and Git snapshot required by ReviewPhase.
WorkerPhase failures retain the existing GotaCycleFailure semantics and cannot start ReviewPhase.

ReviewPhase rejects an incoherent VerifiedWorkerCommit or WorkerPhaseResult with WORKER_RESULT_INVALID before invoking Reviewer; the result is invalid and exposes no decision, including when a wrapper hides a prior Worker failure or omits its handoff.
ReviewPhase validates Reviewer identity, review phase, exact verified SHA, exit status, and post-review Git integrity without executing Worker or writing coordinator state.

Authoritative identity, phase, attempt, SHA, wrapper status, handoff, Git snapshot, and Reviewer decision values require canonical structure, exact runtime types, and exact values; opaque evidence contents remain parser-owned.
The existing GotaReviewCycle remains a composition facade with the same end-to-end public result semantics.

behaviors.precondition: A GotaReviewCycleResult is available from one coordinator cycle.
behaviors.public_action: Call GotaDecisionPolicy.resolve(cycle_result).
behaviors.expected_result: An accepted ReviewDecision maps to COMPLETE, CORRECT, WAIT_FOR_HUMAN, or BLOCK; an invalid cycle produces CYCLE_FAILED without inventing a business decision.
invariants: Only a valid cycle with an accepted ReviewResult can produce a business action.
A technical cycle failure never becomes BLOCK.
Resolution is deterministic and does not execute the selected action or perform Git, Runner, SQLite, TaskRun, or retry work.

behaviors.precondition: A persisted TaskRun is in REVIEW with the active lease and fencing token, and the immutable evidence ledger contains one canonical Worker result, Worker commit verification, and Review result for the same Gota identity.
behaviors.public_action: Call SQLiteCoordinatorStore.transition_gota_to_done() with the run ID and active lease.
behaviors.expected_result: The store accepts only REVIEW -> DONE after validating the persisted Gota evidence, exact Worker and reviewed commit SHA, and PASSED decision; it appends one store-generated gota_acceptance_verified evidence record in the same transaction.
invariants: Expired or stale leases, mismatched fencing tokens, non-REVIEW states, missing or incoherent evidence, and non-PASSED decisions reject without acceptance evidence.
The acceptance evidence digest, timestamp, identity references, and fencing token are generated and persisted by the store rather than supplied by the caller.
A failure after validation rolls back both gota_acceptance_verified and the REVIEW -> DONE state change.
A second call from DONE creates no evidence, transition event, or repeated state change.
The boundary performs no Git mutation and does not call the legacy acceptance path.

behaviors.precondition: A canonical WorkerResult is available for a RUNNING or REVIEW TaskRun with its active lease and fencing token.
behaviors.public_action: Call SQLiteCoordinatorStore.persist_gota_worker_result() and later load_gota_worker_result() for the exact run, attempt, and request identity.
behaviors.expected_result: The complete canonical WorkerResult survives SQLite restart as one immutable gota_worker_result_received authority, or absence remains explicit when no result was persisted.
invariants: The persisted payload is the flujo.gota/v1 canonical WorkerResult, including identity, result, commit_sha, changed_paths, evidence, and checkpoint.
The store generates the evidence ID, digest, fencing token, and trusted timestamp; generic callers cannot append gota_worker_result_received.
An identical retry is idempotent, a conflicting or duplicated authority fails closed, and tampering or incoherent identity is rejected.
Git state never fabricates or substitutes a missing WorkerResult, and stale or expired fencing is rejected.

behaviors.precondition: A worker-phase GotaRequest is canonical, its TaskRun is RUNNING with an active lease, and the store has no reservation for that run, attempt, and request identity.
behaviors.public_action: Call SQLiteCoordinatorStore.reserve_gota_worker_invocation() before invoking WorkerPhase.
behaviors.expected_result: One atomic store transaction persists the complete canonical Worker request and one invocation-start authority; later calls reuse a durable WorkerResult or fail closed without invoking Worker again.
invariants: Request and invocation marker are committed together or neither is durable.
The request retains every flujo.gota/v1 WorkerRequest field and reloads through the canonical request parser.
A same-identity request is idempotent, a conflicting request is rejected without overwrite, and tampering or duplicate authorities fail closed.
Generic append_evidence cannot create either reserved authority, including with str subclasses.
Lease expiry, stale fencing, and a reservation without a WorkerResult never authorize an automatic retry.

behaviors.precondition: A RUNNING TaskRun has one intact durable Worker request, invocation reservation, and READY_FOR_REVIEW WorkerResult for the same attempt and request identity.
behaviors.public_action: Call GotaWorkerReviewBoundary.run() with the run identity and active lease.
behaviors.expected_result: The boundary independently revalidates the durable Worker commit through the existing read-only Git verifier, atomically records one reserved gota_worker_commit_verified authority plus one Gota-specific boundary anchor linking its exact evidence digest and transition event, and transitions RUNNING to REVIEW without executing Worker or Reviewer.
invariants: The durable request, reservation, WorkerResult, active lease, and fencing token are revalidated inside the final SQLite transaction.
The WorkerResult commit SHA remains the primary authority; Git only verifies it, including ancestry, exactly-one-commit, clean worktree, branch, refs fingerprint, and exact changed paths.

A Git verification failure, missing or incoherent durable authority, expired lease, stale fence, final fencing failure, or SQLite failure leaves RUNNING without new commit-verification evidence, a boundary anchor, or a REVIEW event.

REVIEW requires exactly one coherent commit-verification evidence record, one Gota-specific boundary anchor for run/attempt/request, and the exact anchored transition event with matching evidence ID, digest, fencing, and timestamp.
The final trusted lease/fencing check occurs after the anchor and last Git verification; any failure rolls back the complete frontier transaction.

A repeated call revalidates the anchored evidence, transition event, links, and current Git fingerprint read-only; it is idempotent and does not execute Worker or duplicate evidence, events, or the anchor.
The boundary invokes only the read-only Git adapter and never invokes Reviewer, ReviewResult persistence, DecisionPolicy, or transition_gota_to_done.

FIX-REVIEW-TAKEOVER-001: historical Worker request/invocation/result share one positive fence; REVIEW commit verification and its anchored transition share their own positive fence, never older than Worker authority. Reentry after takeover before or after REVIEW preserves both generations and never repeats Worker or duplicates the frontier; only the current valid lease authorizes new mutations.
behaviors.notes: FIX-REVIEW-TAKEOVER-001 corrects existing recovery behavior, not a behavior-preserving refactor. The new pre-REVIEW takeover/reentry regression reproduced the exact transition event incoherence against unchanged production; prior takeover coverage stopped after first REVIEW entry. Explicit fencing tampering variants protect fail-closed validation.

behaviors.precondition: A TaskRun is in REVIEW with one intact durable Worker request, reservation, WorkerResult, and anchored Worker-to-Review frontier for the same attempt.
behaviors.public_action: Call GotaReviewerPersistenceBoundary.run() with the active lease and Worker request identity.
behaviors.expected_result: The existing ReviewPhase reviews exactly the durable Worker commit, and one complete canonical ReviewResult is persisted with an independent evidence anchor while the TaskRun remains REVIEW.
invariants: Worker-to-Review is revalidated before Reviewer and again before ReviewResult persistence.
A missing ReviewResult permits a later read-only retry on the same durable Worker SHA; an intact ReviewResult suppresses Reviewer execution.
The gota_review_result evidence and its anchor share one trusted timestamp, and the anchor fixes the evidence ID, evidence digest, and real gota_worker_commit_verified evidence ID.
Tampering, duplicate or conflicting authorities, stale leases, stale fencing, and Git changes fail closed without changing REVIEW or creating terminal evidence.

behaviors.precondition: A TaskRun has one intact durable Worker-to-Review frontier and one canonical ReviewResult for the same Gota attempt.
behaviors.public_action: Call GotaDecisionApplicationBoundary.run() with the active lease and the durable Gota identity.
behaviors.expected_result: GotaDecisionPolicy resolves the durable ReviewResult and the boundary applies COMPLETE through the store acceptance primitive, or atomically applies CORRECT, WAIT_FOR_HUMAN, or BLOCK without rerunning Worker or Reviewer.
invariants: Only durable Worker and Review authorities supply the Policy input; the boundary does not map ReviewDecision values independently.
PASSED creates exactly one store-generated gota_acceptance_verified authority and a REVIEW -> DONE event; a repeated call recognizes the complete frontier read-only.
Non-PASSED actions preserve atomic state, decision evidence, human hold, lease, fencing, trusted-clock, rollback, and restart-idempotence guarantees.
Incomplete, duplicate, tampered, stale, expired, or legacy authorities fail closed, and CYCLE_FAILED is not materialized from an intact durable ReviewResult.

behaviors.area: Self-contained verified Gota semantic review packet
behaviors.precondition: The existing Coordinator Git verifier accepts a coherent Worker handoff or durable Worker-to-Review frontier.
behaviors.public_action: Run ReviewPhase, optionally through GotaReviewerPersistenceBoundary.
behaviors.expected_result: Reviewer receives the exact Coordinator-read patch and commit metadata, verified Git facts, request criteria and paths, and separately identified complete Worker reports and persisted evidence bodies without shell or external evidence reads.
invariants: Only the existing Coordinator Git verifier establishes commit, ancestry, exactly-one-commit, changed paths and clean worktree authority; Worker claims never replace it.
Packet construction checks the Git fingerprint before Reviewer and existing post-review verification remains mandatory.
The complete binary/full-index patch preserves final newlines and is never silently truncated; diff-check findings remain explicit.
SHA/path incoherence or failed packet Git inspection never starts Reviewer.
Canonical Reviewer allows only read, glob and grep; shell, edit, external_directory, subagent and skill remain denied and no model is fixed.
ReviewResult persistence and DecisionApplication keep their existing anchors, fencing and restart guarantees.
behaviors.notes: Authorized behavior correction FIX-REVIEW-ACCESS-001, not a behavior-preserving refactor. Four new focal tests failed against unchanged production before implementation. DecisionApplication historical failing status corrected after a fresh passing baseline. Real-agent discovery/no-tool smoke is delivery evidence, not implied by these unit test paths.
